title: 2023 HMMT February Guts Problem 8
statement: Suppose \(a, b\), and \(c\) are distinct positive integers such that \(\sqrt{a \sqrt{b \sqrt{c}}}\) is an integer. Compute the least possible value of \(a+b+c\).

solutions.text: First, check that no permutation of \((1,2,3)\) works, so the sum must be more than 6 . Then since \((a, b, c)=(2,4,1)\) has \(\sqrt{2 \sqrt{4 \sqrt{1}}}=2\), the answer must be \(2+4+1=7\).
